name: Nova Trading Platform
tag: Lets strategy and risk agents test trading ideas and size positions, with a live portfolio view.

scenarios.title: Test a strategy with risk limits
scenarios.ask: Test a {strategy} strategy on a ${=account} sample account, risking {=risk}% per trade.
steps: Strategy agent
Set entry and exit rules for {strategy} on a sample of 40 liquid stocks.
Backtester
Replayed five years of sample price history. Illustrative win rate: {=strategy}%.
Risk agent
Sized each trade so a stop-out loses ${=round(account * risk / 100)} or less.
Portfolio agent
Capped total open risk at 6% of the account, or {=floor(6 / risk)} full-size positions at once.
Reporter
Labeled every number as a backtest illustration with costs and slippage estimated.

result.title: Backtest summary (illustration)
rows: About {=round((14 - strategy / 7) * risk, 1)}% of the account
Past results do not predict future results. Not financial advice.

followups: Is a higher win rate always better?
No. Mean reversion often wins more often but with smaller gains per trade. What matters is win rate together with average win and average loss.
A stop-out would cost ${=round(account * 0.02)}, and the same losing streak would take about {=round((14 - strategy / 7) * 2, 1)}% off the account.
Can it place trades for me?
It can send orders to a connected broker, but only after you approve each one, and the risk agent blocks orders that break your limits.

scenarios.title: Check portfolio risk
scenarios.ask: Review my {positions} open positions. The largest is {=largest}% of the portfolio. Flag risks.
steps: Portfolio agent
Loaded {positions} positions across {sectors} sectors from the live view.
Concentration check
The largest position is {=largest}% against a sample limit of 15%.
Correlation check
About {=min(positions, max(2, round(positions / sectors)))} positions tend to move together in the sample data.
Risk agent
Listed changes that would bring the portfolio inside your limits, for you to review.

result.title: Risk review (illustration)
rows: Educational check only. Not financial advice.

followups: Where does the 15% limit come from?
It is a sample setting. You set your own limits per position, sector and total risk, and the checks use those.
No. It suggests changes and shows their effect. Nothing trades without your approval.

scenarios.title: Prepare the morning watchlist
scenarios.ask: Scan my {watch} watchlist names before the open and tell me which match my {strategy} setups.
steps: Data agent
Pulled overnight prices and news for {watch} names.
Signal agent
{=max(1, round(watch * strategy / 100))} names match your {strategy} rules.
Risk agent
Removed names with earnings in the next two days.
Reporter
Sorted the remaining names by how close they are to an entry level.
followups: You write the rules in plain terms, like price above the 50-day average and volume above normal. The Signal agent turns them into checks you can read and edit.
No. It is a short list to research. Decisions stay with you, and nothing here is financial advice.
